svg.aria-label: How to write ぱ: 4 strokes · 3 pen lifts · 7 movements
svg.title: Writing ぱ
svg.desc: 7 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of ぱ (japanese), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansJP-Subset.ttf. Stroke order after KanjiVG, kanji/03071.svg, hiragana ぱ (U+3071 HIRAGANA LETTER PA), four stroke paths kvg:03071-s1 to s4 (Ulrich Apel and contributors, CC BY-SA 3.0) <https://github.com/KanjiVG/kanjivg/blob/master/kanji/03071.svg>. Source note on variation: KanjiVG stores each stroke as one directed path in writing order: s1 to s3 are は's strokes, the same paths as in its file for は, kanji/0306f.svg; s4 is the handakuten, one closed ring that starts at its foot and runs clockwise, round the left side, over the top and down the right side back to the foot. Only the order and direction are taken from that file. The learner path's coordinates are the bundled Noto Sans JP outline's own medial line, so the print glyph's proportions, not KanjiVG's handwriting-style ones, decide where each stroke runs. Where the print glyph's left vertical runs on below the point the flick leaves it, the path goes down to the foot of that ink and climbs back a short way before the flick.
svg.text: How it is written — 4 strokes · 3 pen lifts · 7 movements
Stroke order after KanjiVG, kanji/03071.svg, hiragana ぱ (U+3071 HIRAGANA LETTER PA), four stroke paths kvg:03071-s1 to s4 (Ulrich Apel and contributors, CC BY-SA 3.0)
This order is attested, not standardised; the source records where it varies.
